messages.text: 10k sample this is
Understood—10k electrons. I’ll use the standard 10k configuration and check what is needed for a valid before/after gap comparison.

The routing prototype leaves the calorimeter positions unchanged, so it cannot yet demonstrate a smaller gap. I’ll test the proposed reduction from an 800 mm to a 400 mm warm gap as an isolated sensitivity study, with the same 10k electron inputs, sampling and readout. This will measure the potential response gain; the unresolved service interfaces will remain explicit.

I’m using the repository’s validation workflow and the `acts-spack` skill for the run.

The node preflight still reports changed Spack setup/lock fingerprints. I’ll verify the installed runtime directly before simulation, without changing shared dependencies. The comparison will be ECAL-only at zero field, using the existing 10k primary records.

The published 10k reference passed its saved-data and provenance checks: all events, worker audits, primary inputs, libraries and component sources are intact. I can reuse it as the 800 mm reference and run the new 400 mm candidate.

The geometry check also confirms that the two endcaps must move independently toward the interaction point; their local readout coordinates and internal construction stay fixed.

The comparison will use the same 999 electrons in the fixed \(|\eta|=1.2–1.5\) transition region, plus finer bins to show whether the response dip moves. I’ve also fixed a common low-response threshold from the reference, so the new sample will be judged against the same threshold.

The candidate preserves the existing endcap absorber, liquid argon, cryostat and local services. Before the 10k run, I’m checking the complete signed placement change, overlaps and a short serial-versus-multithread control to make sure the simulation remains consistent.

The helper tests passed, including checks for wrong shifts, changed readout or material, and mismatched serial/MT data. I’m freezing the candidate source and starting native construction and overlap checks, followed by the short transport controls. The 10k run will follow if those gates pass.

The first native audit stopped before any showers: its calculation of material remaining inside a reusable period mother returned a negative volume. The independent software review flagged the same issue with ROOT’s Boolean-solid volume estimates. I’ll correct the audit method before continuing.

Both reviews agree on the correction: compare every native solid definition, material recipe and placement transform, and retain the existing analytic material inventory. That will verify conservation under the rigid move while keeping the 10 nm overlap gate unchanged. The failed audit is preserved for provenance.

The corrected audit passes for the standard geometry: 290,216 physical placements checked, with zero overlaps at 10 nm. The smaller-gap geometry is now going through the same check; the serial/MT control and pilot follow next.

Both geometries now pass the native checks. All 82,598 endcap descendant placements follow the expected translation, and both models have zero overlaps at 10 nm. The 24-event serial run and saved-data readback passed; the multithread comparison and 100-event pilot are next.

The serial/MT control agrees exactly on all 20,023 saved cells, including energies and positions. The 100-event pilot and its readback also passed. The full 10k-electron candidate run is now running on twelve workers; afterward I’ll audit every saved event and compare it with the verified 800 mm reference.
The full run is progressing: about 900 primary IDs have started and the output is growing. I’m keeping the fixed transition bins and all-event denominators unchanged for the final comparison.

The run has reached roughly 1,900 of 10,000 primary IDs. The source remains frozen, and the independent software review has closed both audit findings. The full saved-data check and response comparison will follow once transport finishes.

The long run has exposed rare endcap hit-assignment errors at radial boundaries. The saved standard reference contains the same error class. I’m checking whether any deposited energy is lost before treating the response comparison as validated; the current run will be retained as diagnostic evidence.

The diagnosis confirms that positive-energy steps can be omitted: their midpoint falls inside an annulus hole and fails cell assignment. I’ll add independent step-energy accounting and replay both 10k variants with the geometry and readout unchanged. That will quantify the omitted energy and let us assess the gap response without inventing valid cells for those deposits.

The first 10k saved-hit comparison shows a substantial improvement in the fixed transition region: SD/mean falls from **44.2% to 21.0%**. Globally it falls from **17.8% to 13.6%**. These are provisional results; the independent energy accounting will quantify the omitted deposits before I finalize the comparison.

The independent recorder now compiles. Its checks will reconcile native step energy with saved cell energies, including the output’s float rounding. Omitted deposits will remain explicitly unassigned in the readout; the comparison will show both saved-hit and complete active-deposit response.

The observer’s short controls are now running in both geometries from a clean committed source. Each will be checked against the saved cell data before the full replays. The 800 mm and 400 mm detector descriptions remain unchanged.

The recorder passes the serial and multithread checks in both geometries: each saved cell energy agrees with the independent successful-step sum. The 100-event pilots are finishing. I’m also adding the reviewer’s missing map-artifact check before the full replays.

Both 100-event pilots passed, the corrected artifact check passed, and the independent review has closed the observer findings. The full 10k replays are now running for both geometries, with complete step-energy accounting alongside the existing hit readout.

Both replays have started roughly 1,800–1,900 primaries. The recorder has captured the first unassigned-step cases with their event identities, so the final audit can measure their energy contribution rather than infer it from the interleaved logs.

The replays have reached about 6,800 standard-gap and 6,400 smaller-gap primary IDs. The observer is retaining the rare omitted contributions with their event and track identities. Once transport finishes, the remaining checks are full energy closure, replay equality and the final paired comparison.

Transport is near the end: about 9,300 standard-gap and 8,800 smaller-gap primaries have started. The observer has captured the same three and two rare error cases seen in the retained runs. The full-population energy and cell-replay audits follow next.
Both 10k simulations have finished transport. I’m now checking complete energy accounting and confirming that the saved hits reproduce the retained runs exactly before finalizing the comparison.

The replay receipts confirm 10,000 events per geometry with unchanged simulation sources and libraries. The audit is still reading the full hit files; it will quantify the rare unassigned deposits separately from the gap response.

Independent software review has cleared the readback correction. It matches all three standard-gap and two smaller-gap failures to the native geometry without changing cell lookup or its tolerances. Full energy closure and replay checks are still running.

All 20,000 replayed primaries passed saved-data readback. The corrected auditor is now checking each saved cell against its accumulated steps and comparing every event with the retained run. That will establish whether the gap improvement survives complete deposit accounting.

I’m packaging the comparison with its input hashes, reproduction commands, and token/work records for a separate draft PR. The study tests an 800→400 mm warm-gap reduction; service-interface engineering remains a separate requirement.

The standard-gap audit has passed per-cell and energy closure for all 10,000 events; the smaller-gap audit is close behind. The remaining check is exact saved-hit replay against each retained run, followed by the uncertainty calculation and plots.

Energy accounting now closes for every event in both samples. Unassigned deposits total 1.188 MeV for the standard gap and 0.149 MeV for the smaller gap across 10,000 electrons each. They are recorded separately; exact replay verification is still finishing.

The final replay check is still scanning the retained hit files. The geometry and energy checks are complete; I’m waiting for the event-by-event identity result before treating the comparison as final.

Both replay checks passed: every saved event, cell, energy and position matches its retained run, with zero differing events. The complete-energy comparison is now calculating the paired bootstrap intervals; the gap improvement can be assessed independently of the rare hit-assignment losses.

The earlier LAr–SiW results are preserved, with an added note that they report saved-hit energy. The new report will distinguish that quantity from complete sensitive deposits and include the correlations and uncertainties for the gap comparison.

The complete-energy result confirms the improvement: transition SD/mean falls from **44.18% to 21.00%**, and the global value from **17.84% to 13.56%**. The transition reduction is 23.19 percentage points, with a paired 95% interval of 20.60–25.93 points. At the fixed low-response threshold, counts fall from 183 to zero.

The results and plots are ready, and the separate physics reviewer is checking the final evidence. I’m preparing the stacked draft PR with reproducible statistics, material-preservation checks, and work/token records. I’ll use the authenticated GitHub CLI because the connector lacks the required write permission.

Draft [PR #144](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/144) is open and stacked on #143. It contains the audited results, plots and reproduction recipe. I’m finishing the independent physics assessment and its logging closeout before handing it back.

The independent physics review found no actionable issues and reproduced the results, intervals and all 84 covariance variables. Accounting for unassigned energy changes the global gap-width improvement by only about **0.0000034 percentage points**. I’m adding that review and its exact usage record to PR #144.
All local checks pass, and the final review and exact usage records are committed. I’m pushing the closeout to PR #144 and verifying its final head and draft status.

The **10k-electron comparison confirms a substantial improvement** for the conditional 800→400 mm warm-gap reduction.

| Measure | 800 mm | 400 mm |
|---|---:|---:|
| Global raw SD/mean | 17.84% | 13.56% |
| Fixed transition region, 999 electrons | 44.18% | 21.00% |
| Low-response events at the common cut | 183 | 0 |

Complete energy accounting and exact saved-hit replay passed. Independent physics review reproduced the results.

![Gap comparison]([redacted]

[Draft PR #144](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/144) includes results, reproduction commands and token/work records. All 47 focused tests pass; hosted CI is running.

This establishes an **ECAL-only response benefit**. An engineered service installation fitting the smaller gap remains unproven; these raw widths are not intrinsic energy resolution.
